Over the past several months, new technologies and innovative market models have emerged, creating new opportunities for investors, issuers, and market participants.   As this evolution is rapidly moving to an operating reality with live transactions and institutional adoption, Nasdaq is leading the charge in reducing friction, expanding access and making markets more efficient.   Advancing Tokenized Equities: Nasdaq Deepens Relationship with Payward  Nasdaq is advancing its tokenized equities strategy through an agreement to invest $100 million in Payward, the parent company of Kraken. The investment builds on the collaboration announced in March and supports Nasdaq's vision for an equity token framework that places public companies at the center of ownership rights, transparency, and governance.  As part of the expanded relationship, Payward will also adopt Nasdaq's market surveillance technology across its trading venues, helping align market innovation with institutional-grade oversight.  Read more.  Building the Market Infrastructure: DLN Launch and LeveL Markets Acquisition  Nasdaq announced a definitive agreement to acquire LeveL Markets, a leading off-exchange equity execution venue in the United States. The acquisition supports Nasdaq's broader vision for always-on markets by strengthening the way liquidity is connected and accessed across an increasingly continuous global economy.  Nasdaq also launched Digital Liquidity Networks (DLN), bringing together capabilities across digital assets and tokenized securities to help architect the next era of capital markets. Together, these moves represent a significant step toward building the infrastructure required for an always-on market environment.  Learn more.   Tokenized Collateral Goes Live: Vanguard and Wellington Complete First Trades  Roland Chai, President of DLN, announced that Vanguard and Wellington Management completed their first tokenized collateral transactions on the Canton Network. Hey, it's Adrian! Last week I wrote that a correction looked more likely than a breakout. Bitcoin clearly doesn’t read my newsletter. From $76k last Thursday it ran to about $87k by Tuesday, in the same week the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. That’s a real sign of strength. The buyers are back too. The spot ETFs took in about $2.3 billion in four sessions, after losing over $1 billion the week before. Today Bitcoin sits at $83.6k after a flush of long liquidations, right at the price block that held it down for most of the year. I’ve moved to a fully risk-on stance and added leverage to my long term position, because I think we have entered the early bull phase of the cycle. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Market Update – The 10-year yield hit 5.1%, a 19-year high, Brent is back above $105, the Fed hiked and October hike odds jumped to 71%. Bitcoin still ran from $76k to $87k. 🔊 Market Pulse – The June low never broke the Realized Price, the new buyers’ cost basis crossed above the long-term holders’, and ETFs took in about $2.3 billion in four sessions. The next test sits at $95k–$97k. 🐂 Project and Alpha Insights – UNI, HYPE, NEAR and ZEC: what’s working, what’s still missing, and how I’d enter. I added leverage to my Bitcoin position with a liquidation price at $38k, plus a short-term long at $82.3k. The macro state of the market. Market Overview Over the last six months, almost everything that usually hurts Bitcoin has happened: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.1% on Wednesday, the first time in 19 years. It started 2026 at 4.15%. Brent oil is back above $105, and the war in Iran remains unresolved. The Fed hiked last week, and the odds of another hike in October jumped to 75% this week. The CLARITY Act failed in the Senate. AI dystopian panic fantasies is all over the news. Polymarket has the Democrats taking the House at 93% and the Senate at 66% in the November midterms. I’ve written about most of these risks here over the last months. They still didn’t stop me from moving into a fully risk-on stance. Why? Because Bitcoin moves in adoption and market cycles. Who holds it, how the market is structured and how much credit and leverage sits in the system can matter more than the macro. And the macro isn’t only working against Bitcoin.
